title: Perfect quotient reduction as a bounded finite-projective tensor functor
statement: Let T be a scheme, A a commutative ring and d a completed coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. For every positive quotient A/I^(n+1), there exist a bounded cochain complex P of A_T-module sheaves and explicit splittings of each P^j as a retract of a finite power of A_T, together with a natural isomorphism from derived extension along A_T -> (A/I^(n+1))_T followed by exact restriction to the derived tensor-right functor associated to P in [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-tensor-products]. The isomorphism is of functors on all of D(Mod(A_T)), hence preserves their canonical product comparisons.

source.place: proof: Koszul reconstruction and bounded finite-projective quotient representative

proof.text: Perfectness of the quotient in [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] gives a bounded finite-projective A-complex F and an isomorphism in D(A) to the quotient in degree zero. F is K-projective since it is bounded above and termwise projective. Fullness of localization on K-projectives represents that isomorphism by an actual quasi-isomorphism F -> A/I^(n+1)[0].

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction] to this augmentation. Its final clause gives a quasi-isomorphism from the constant complex extended to A_T to the quotient sheaf, the same two degree bounds, and finite-free retracts in each degree. Finite biproduct comparisons replace the finite coproducts by finite products, giving the StrictPerfectCoefficientPackageOnSite required by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-tensor-products].

For every K-flat input C, tensoring with this augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. The balanced tensor cancellation isomorphism identifies tensor with the quotient sheaf with ordinary scalar extension followed by restriction. These comparisons commute with chain maps and homotopies. The universal K-flat left-derived pair in [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and the localization defining finiteProjectiveTensorRight in [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-tensor-products] therefore give the desired natural isomorphism, not merely unrelated objectwise isomorphisms.

lean.statement:
theorem completedFiniteQuotientTensorPresentation (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ (P : CochainComplex (adicDatumModules T d) ℤ)
      (hb : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ j : ℤ, j < a ∨ b < j → IsZero (P.X j))
      (p : SheafOfModules.StrictPerfectCoefficientPackageOnSite
        ((adicLisseForget T).obj (adicDatumRing T d)) P),
      Nonempty (adicDatumReductionUnderlying T d n ≅
        finiteProjectiveTensorRight T d P hb p)
